newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe hit with class action suit.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe hit with class action suit.

text.p: CompuServe Corp. faces a second class action lawsuit for allegedly failing to disclose that the online provider was experiencing adverse trends that affected its growth, the plaintiff's lawyers said Monday.
The latest suit was filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio on behalf of anyone who bought CompuServe stock prior to July 16, 1996.
The plaintiff, Sonia Mitelman, is represented by Strauss & Troy, Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP, and Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz LLP, and other counsel.
The defendants include certain CompuServe officers, parent company H&R Block Inc. and its underwriters.
CompuServe officials were not immediately available for comment.

On July 16, CompuServe projected a loss from operations of up to 20 cents a share for its first fiscal quarter. CompuServe shares fell 81.25 cents to $9.438 on Nasdaq in late trading -- far below the $30 at which they were sold in their initial public offering on April 18, 1996.
CompuServe's underwriters in the IPO, Goldman Sachs & Co., George K. Baum & Co., and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Co., Inc., also were named in the suit.
The plaintiff seeks damages on behalf of anyone who purchased CompuServe's stock on or traceable to its initial public offering, the law firms said.
